module purpose: neorv32_spi accepts bus writes that store control bits or queue 9-bit transmit/control entries, uses programmable clock generation and a shift engine to drive serial clock/data/chip-select outputs, captures received bits into a receive FIFO, returns control/status or received data on the bus response, and raises irq_o from selectable FIFO and idle conditions.

use-case flows.value: controller enable and serial transfer mode/rate settings written into held control fields
interrupt-source enable settings written into held control fields
a transmit/control FIFO entry taken from bus_req_i.data(31) and bus_req_i.data(7 downto 0) and queued for later execution
clock-enable pulses, chip-select commands, and byte shifting that perform a serial transfer and queue the completed received byte
registered interrupt request derived from enabled RX/TX/idle conditions
control/status fields or the next received byte returned on a bus read
control registers, transceiver state, chip-select outputs, interrupt output, and clock-divider state forced to known values when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.enable from bus_req_i.data at line 140. Its integrity matters because this state clears both FIFOs when low (lines 211, 243), gates interrupt generation (line 255), drives the transceiver enable bit in rtx_engine.state (line 281), resets or permits clock generation (lines 369-373), and is exported on clkgen_en_o (line 383). Availability is also established because the bit is held between writes and reset (lines 120, 140).

conceptual assets.concept: Serial transfer timing and polarity configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.cpha, ctrl.cpol, ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.highspeed at lines 141-145. Integrity matters because these held settings determine the serial clock behavior used by the transfer engine: rtx_engine.sck is set from ctrl.cpol and ctrl.cpha at lines 286, 300-301, 309, 320, 324, and 331, while clock_generator uses ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.highspeed to create shift-enable pulses at lines 371-376. Availability is also established because the settings are held and consumed by these computations until rewritten or reset.

The configure flow stores ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf, and ctrl.irq_idle at lines 146-149. Integrity matters because irq_o is asserted only for the enabled conditions in lines 255-259; corrupting these settings changes which RX/TX/idle conditions are reported externally. Availability is also established because the settings are held between writes and reset and are consumed directly by irq_generator.

conceptual assets.concept: Transfer progress state and completion/busy decisions
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow uses rtx_engine.state to step through the transfer phases (lines 293, 303, 312, 322, 325), increments rtx_engine.bitcnt on each enabled shift (line 311), asserts rtx_engine.done when the last bit is reached (lines 319-322), and derives rtx_engine.busy from the state low bits (line 340). Integrity matters because these values decide when the engine fetches a queued entry (line 214 and lines 288-293), when shifting continues, when a received byte is committed to the RX FIFO through rtx_engine.done (line 245), and when idle status is reported (lines 172, 259). Availability is established while ctrl.enable is active and spi_clk_en pulses occur (lines 281, 299, 308, 317).

conceptual assets.concept: Clock-generation state and driven serial clock level
conceptual assets.reasoning: clock_generator clears or advances cdiv_cnt and asserts spi_clk_en when the programmed divider count is reached (lines 369-376). The transceiver only updates rtx_engine.sck when spi_clk_en is high (lines 299, 308, 317), and spi_clk_o copies rtx_engine.sck at line 344. Integrity matters because wrong divider state, enable pulses, or clock level changes when the external serial clock toggles. Availability is established under ctrl.enable and the selected clock source condition at line 371.

conceptual assets.concept: Transferred byte in the shift engine
conceptual assets.reasoning: When a data entry is fetched, rtx_engine.sreg is loaded from tx_fifo.rdata(7 downto 0) at line 292 and transfer starts at line 293. During shifting, spi_dat_i is sampled into rtx_engine.sdi_sync at line 310 and shifted into rtx_engine.sreg at line 318; spi_dat_o is driven from rtx_engine.sreg(7) at line 343. The completed byte is then presented to the RX FIFO input at lines 244-245. Integrity matters because corrupting this stored byte changes both the serial data driven out and the byte queued after reception. Availability is established while queued data is available and spi_clk_en advances the shift (lines 288, 308, 317).

A fetched control entry selects chip-select behavior: line 289 tests tx_fifo.rdata(8), and line 290 stores tx_fifo.rdata(3 downto 0) into rtx_engine.cs_ctrl. chip_select then drives all chip-select outputs inactive and asserts exactly one selected line low when rtx_engine.cs_ctrl(3) is high (lines 352-355). Integrity matters because this state chooses which external target is addressed. Availability is conditional on a control entry being fetched and remains until cleared by line 332 or reset.

irq_generator registers irq_o from ctrl.enable and the enabled status conditions at lines 255-259: rx_fifo.avail, not tx_fifo.avail, not tx_fifo.half, and idle defined by not tx_fifo.avail and not rtx_engine.busy. Integrity matters because irq_o is the module's external event report. Availability is established on each rising edge when reset is inactive and an enabled condition holds (lines 252-255).
